name: APEMAGA
rootCause: The family() function enables anyone to burn the token balance of any arbitrary user without authorization. Internally, it calls the _*approve_*() function with account as both owner and spender, but without verifying the caller’s identity. This allows an attacker to reduce the token balance of critical addresses (e.g., a DEX pair) to near zero, enabling price manipulation and draining of liquidity pools via favorable swap conditions. Vulnerable code snippet: Attack tx: https://app.blocksec.com/explorer/tx/eth/0x6beb21b53f5b205c088570333ec875b720e333b49657f7026b01ed72b026851e?line=19 Analysis: The family function doesn’t authenticate the identity of msg.sender and owner. As a result, anyone can burn other’s token balance without their approval. The attacker call family(pair) several times, to reduce the token.balanceOf(pair) to a minimum amount, causing the price to be manipulated. Thus, he can drain the pair contract with a normal swap.

APEMAGA on Ethereum suspected to have been attacked, resulting in a loss of approximately $32,000.

APEMAGA was exploited within hours of launch on Ethereum Mainnet, resulting in an estimated $32,000 loss. The attack drained the contract's APEMAGA token reserves, but the precise vulnerable mechanism in the deployed contract is not available. Proof-of-concept code and on-chain evidence suggest the loss was realized through liquidity pair manipulation and token swaps. A business logic flaw allowed an attacker to manipulate liquidity pair reserves via repeated custom function calls and synchronize operations.
